records.answer: There is no `itertools.chunked_window()` in the Python standard library; you may be thinking of `itertools.batched()` (Python 3.12+), which yields successive tuples of up to *n* items, or of `more_itertools.chunked()` / `more_itertools.windowed()` from the third-party `more-itertools` package.

There is no `itertools.chunked_window()` in the Python standard library, so calling it raises an `AttributeError`; you may be thinking of `itertools.batched(iterable, n)` (Python 3.12+), which yields successive non-overlapping tuples of up to `n` items, or the third-party `more_itertools.windowed()`, which yields overlapping sliding windows.

There is no `itertools.chunked_window()` in the Python standard library; you may be thinking of `itertools.batched(iterable, n)` (Python 3.12+), which returns an iterator of tuples of up to *n* consecutive items, or the third-party `more_itertools.windowed()`/`chunked()` functions, which yield sliding windows or lists of consecutive items respectively.

There is no `itertools.chunked_window()` in the Python standard library; you may be thinking of `itertools.batched(iterable, n)` (Python 3.12+), which returns tuples of up to `n` consecutive items, `itertools.pairwise()`, which returns overlapping pairs, or the third-party `more_itertools.windowed()`/`chunked()`.

There is no `itertools.chunked_window()` in the Python standard library; you may be thinking of `itertools.batched(iterable, n)` (Python 3.12+), which returns an iterator of tuples of up to *n* consecutive items, or of the `sliding_window` recipe in the itertools docs (or `more_itertools.windowed`/`chunked`), which produce overlapping windows or list chunks.
